chunks: And as for what was narrated - Musa from Abbas from Aban from al-Halabi, Ubayd Allah, who said:
A boy moved a basket and broke two eggs in the Haram (sanctuary), so I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he said, 'Two lambs or two young goats.'

This is not contradictory to what we presented earlier, because this report is understood to mean that if the egg is one in which the chick has already moved, then at that time it is obligatory upon him to pay the ransom of a sheep or a young goat or a lamb.
And if the chick had not moved in it, the value (of the egg) is obligatory upon him according to what we presented earlier.
And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca/Medina where Ihram rules apply)
key_terms.جَدْيَانِ: Two young goats (a specific type of ransom animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the fidya (ransom) for breaking an egg while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi utilizes this narration from Aban ibn Taghlib to resolve apparent contradictions in the fiqh of Ihram by distinguishing between eggs with a developing fetus (requiring a fixed fidya of a sheep or goat) and empty eggs (requiring monetary compensation). This contextualization highlights the Shia scholarly method of harmonizing diverse hadiths through specific conditions, ensuring the ruling aligns with the principle of proportional liability for accidental transgressions during pilgrimage.
